hero.title: Taking Robotics to the Community
hero.subtitle: We don't wait for people to find FIRST — we bring the robot to libraries, schools, and community events across Elmbrook so students and families can see student-built robotics up close.

impact.label: Our Approach
impact.text: Community demos turn 'never heard of robotics' into 'I want to try that.' We show up where families already are — the library, a club fair, a district STEM expo — and put GEarheads in front of kids who'd otherwise never see this. Every demo is hands-on: students drive the robot, ask us anything, and leave knowing what building one from scratch actually feels like.

approach.label: Why We Show Up
approach.heading: Robotics Shouldn't Require Seeking It Out
approach.body:
The kids who'd thrive in an engineering program are often the ones who never knew it existed. So we set up where families already go — the library, the club fair, the district STEM showcase. No application, no prior knowledge, no commitment. Just a robot doing something unexpected somewhere you already were.

The robot moves, members explain what they built, and parents get a straight answer about what an FTC season takes. Younger kids get a glimpse of where an FLL kit or a coding class can lead.

Add it up over a season and hundreds of Elmbrook students have watched us run a robot. So when a friend mentions robotics later, the name rings a bell. Low overhead, high reach — that's why we keep showing up.

venues.title: Brookfield Public Library
venues.description: Our most interactive event. We bring the full competition robot into the main community room and let attendees drive it through sample tasks. Librarians promote it on their programming calendar, so we reach kids curious about STEM who haven't found a club yet. Members explain the drivetrain, intake, and launcher in plain language, and parents get a frank answer about what an FTC season takes.

venues.title: Elm Grove Public Library
venues.description: A smaller, tighter-knit crowd than Brookfield, where families already know each other. We run a condensed version — robot demo, Q&A, a table of handouts — which leaves more time for one-on-one talks about programming and what build-season Saturdays actually look like. Staff are generous with space and scheduling, so we're back every season.

venues.title: Brookfield Central Club Fair
venues.description: Our biggest recruiting moment of the year — the one event where incoming freshmen are actually deciding what clubs to join. We run a full booth: robot on display, match footage playing, handouts, members fielding questions. Hundreds of students pass through in a morning, so we keep the robot moving and run quick demos to catch as many as we can.

venues.title: Elmbrook Education Foundation STEM Fairs
venues.description: District-wide STEM programming reaching a younger, broader audience than our high school events. Here we're more showcase than recruiter — bringing the robot and sometimes CAD printouts or notebook pages to show what years of FIRST can build toward. Foundation staff connect us with teachers and administrators across the district, and it's part of why Elmbrook Schools backs us with sponsorship.
